transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-02-18
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (RW AE), Ethan Park (RW SE), Laura Mitchell (Crestview Head Eng), Raj Patel (CISO), Tanya Gomez (ML Platform), Samir Desai (Procurement)

Summary: Quick scoping for a security-focused pilot to validate Redwood Dedicated/Private options. Customer wants SOC 2 + ISO evidence, SSO/SAML integration, fine-grained RBAC, and tamper-evident audit logs. Also need workload sizing to estimate reserved capacity for pilot and benchmarks for latency/cost tradeoffs.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining; quick rollcall?
[00:05] Laura Mitchell: Hey, Laura here.
[00:07] Raj Patel: Raj, CISO.
[00:09] Tanya Gomez: Tanya.
[00:10] Samir Desai: Samir from procurement.
[00:13] Maya Chen: Great, I'm Maya, AE, with Ethan our SE. We'll keep this to 45ish minutes, go over scoping and security requirements for the pilot.
[00:22] Ethan Park: Hi all, quick agenda: success criteria, estimated workload / sizing, benchmarks we plan to run, security controls (SOC 2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs), timeline and next steps.
[00:34] Laura Mitchell: Sounds good; our primary goal is to validate the model quality and latency under our peak loads, but security gating is the big blocker. We need to confirm you can meet our compliance and integration needs before we sign off on pilot resources.
[00:50] Raj Patel: To be specific: we need SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 evidence, formal attestation if possible, SSO via SAML or OIDC to integrate with our Okta, RBAC at team and route-level, encryption in transit + at rest with customer-managed KMS ideally, and immutable audit logs with retention options.
[01:15] Ethan Park: Understood. For SOC 2/ISO we can share our latest reports and a security pack. For SSO, Redwood supports SAML and OIDC; we have template metadata and the SE can help with assertion attributes mapping. We also support RBAC—roles, groups, and route permissions in Console and via API.
[01:36] Raj Patel: How does RBAC map to model routing? We don't want devs accidentally hitting prod models or sending data to hosted endpoints.
[01:44] Ethan Park: You can pin projects to Dedicated clusters or Private deployment; RBAC can restrict who can create routes or deploy model versions. For hosted API we have access keys and project-level isolation, but for the security pilot you might prefer Dedicated or Private so data never leaves your VPC.
[02:05] Laura Mitchell: Data residency — we need data to stay in our us-west-2 region and be retained for 30 days only. Can you configure that?
[02:13] Maya Chen: Yes, for Private and Dedicated we can specify region and retention. We'll capture that as an action item.
[02:20] Raj Patel: Audit logs — what granularity and can we ship logs to our SIEM?
[02:25] Ethan Park: We provide request-level audit logs: request metadata, model version, user id, route, timestamp, and tokens usage. Logs can be exported to S3, CloudWatch, or pushed to your SIEM via our streaming connector. We can also sign logs with tamper-evidence and offer an immutable storage option for compliance.
[02:45] Raj Patel: That's good. On encryption, can you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?
[02:50] Ethan Park: Yes, for Private deployments we support KMS/HSM integration. For Dedicated, we support KMS integrations per customer. For hosted, we manage keys unless you choose a private deployment.
[03:05] Laura Mitchell: Okay, on the success criteria side: we need p95 latency under 500ms for short prompts (<256 tokens) and throughput to handle bursts to 10k reqs/day with sustained 2k qps? (laughs) I mean sustained 200 qps.
[03:25] Ethan Park: We'll need to size the Dedicated pool; rough back-of-envelope: for a 256-token p95 target we recommend N GPU cores depending on model. If you share sample prompt distribution and concurrency profile we'll run an initial perf estimate and a benchmark.
[03:44] Tanya Gomez: We'll provide the top 10 prompt patterns and estimated concurrency. Also note we have redaction rules — PII must be masked before logs are stored.
[03:55] Ethan Park: We support configurable redaction pipelines and can filter or hash PII in transit before writing to audit logs. We'll include that in the design doc.
[04:10] Samir Desai: Procurement question — what's the expected cost for a month-long pilot and do you do reserved capacity?
[04:17] Maya Chen: We typically offer a 3-week pilot on a small Dedicated cluster with the option to extend; we'll provide pricing ranges and a one-page SOW. If you need reserved capacity we can estimate based on the workload.
[04:30] Laura Mitchell: Timeline — we want pilot kickoff within 3 weeks pending security review. Can you meet that?
[04:37] Ethan Park: Yes, assuming we get SOC docs and SSO metadata and you provide the sample workload. We'll need approvals from your infra to open peering or set up a VPC connector for Private.
[04:50] Raj Patel: Regarding SSO — what's the flow for mapping Okta groups to RBAC roles?
[04:56] Ethan Park: We map SAML groups to Redwood roles and have SCIM for provisioning users. We can share a runbook for Okta attributes and sample configuration.
[05:10] Laura Mitchell: Benchmarks — what's the nature of the tests you'll run?
[05:14] Ethan Park: We'll run a benchmark harness: synthetic replay of your prompts with real token lengths, measure p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, and cost per 1k tokens. We'll also test failure modes and fallback routing — e.g., if Dedicated is saturated, we can failover to a compatible variant if you allow it.
[05:36] Laura Mitchell: For pilot success, we'll evaluate on: 1) security/compliance check cleared, 2) latency & throughput meeting p95 target, 3) quality regression within acceptable bounds vs baseline, 4) integration completeness (SSO, audit logs).
[05:55] Ethan Park: Great — we'll put those success criteria in the SOW.
[06:02] Raj Patel: Any red flags around regulatory compliance? We handle PHI; we need to ensure there are BAA conversations if PHI is in scope.
[06:11] Maya Chen: Noted. If PHI is in-scope we'll escalate to enterprise legal and discuss BAA and Private on-prem options. We'll capture that as an action item.
[06:22] Laura Mitchell: On the sample dataset — we'll send a sanitized subset of records for the benchmark. Expect to see variable prompt lengths and some multi-turn prompts.
[06:31] Ethan Park: That's perfect. Also, for cost controls during pilot we can enable quotas and token caps per route to avoid surprise usage.
[06:39] Samir Desai: For procurement we need a PO template and payment terms.
[06:43] Maya Chen: We'll attach a standard PO template and proposed net-30 terms; procurement will send back if they need different terms.
[06:50] Laura Mitchell: Any dependencies from our side?
[06:52] Ethan Park: SSO metadata, sample prompts, infra contact for VPC peering (if Private), and a list of users to provision for RBAC.
[07:01] Raj Patel: Also want to run an initial security deep-dive with your security team — can we schedule that next week?
[07:06] Maya Chen: Yes, Ethan will coordinate.
[07:09] Ethan Park: I'll send a calendar invite for the security deep-dive and include the SE/infra folks.
[07:16] Laura Mitchell: Great.
[07:17] Maya Chen: Recap — action items: we'll send SOC/ISO docs, run perf estimate after sample workload, send SOW and pricing, customer to send sample prompts and confirm timeline.
[07:29] Samir Desai: Sounds good. Any final questions?
[07:32] Raj Patel: None for now.
[07:34] Laura Mitchell: No. Thanks everyone.
[07:36] Maya Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up with docs + action items.

Attachments / references mentioned: security pack (SOC2/ISO links), SOW template (link), benchmark harness doc (link), Okta runbook (link).

End of transcript.
